# Player-owned cumulative token policy

`TaskJournal::budget_configure` is a dedicated player-only host entry point. It is deliberately absent from `budget_call` and all model proxy/tool allowlists. Main routes `budget.configure` only after the native player gateway captures project/session/world identity.

Input: `{projectId,sessionId,worldId,taskId,generation,operationId,maxTokens}`. Unknown fields are rejected. `maxTokens` is required, null for unlimited cumulative tokens or an integer from 1 through 9007199254740991. The current session workspace head, world, task binding and generation must match. A current running, finished, cancelled or interrupted task can be configured without opening a new task, granting a write lease or replaying a model request. Superseded tasks cannot configure a successor.

Output: `{operationId,budget,previousMaxTokens}`. The full request and original output are transactionally audited in `craftmine_budget_configurations`, keyed by budget owner and operation ID. Identical retries return the original receipt; changed inputs fail. Configuration preserves the budget owner, generation, every known usage, unknown reservation, request count, compaction count, deadline and draft. Setting a limit below charged usage is allowed; the next reservation fails without deleting usage. Cached input tokens remain real usage.

New owners default to `limits.maxTokens:null` and `remainingTokens:null`. Model context capacity and maximum output remain separate. Independent request, compaction and deadline boundaries remain enforced. Reserve cannot replace an already fixed limit. Player configuration can change only the cumulative token field.

Migration holds an immediate SQLite transaction across checking/creating the configuration table and preserving existing owners' prior default (1000000 when missing). Existing stored policies are unchanged. Backup schema 3 includes the audit table. Schemas 1 and 2 are validated against their exact legacy shape and upgraded in memory with empty audit history and the old finite default for old owners missing limits/runtime rows. Schema 1 also retains the prior memory-receipt migration. Unknown future versions are rejected. No model/account credentials are included.

Validation: actual Rust database tests exercise unlimited reservations above one million, independent request/compaction exhaustion, cancellation/interruption and recovery with unknown usage, identical/different replays, foreign identities, invalid limits, unavailable model dispatcher entry, atomic upgrade and process reopen, legacy backup restoration, schema-3 audit inclusion and future-version rejection. Native UI/gateway authorization is validated by the integrating parent; Rust does not infer a human from a caller-supplied flag.

First-request deadline initialization is a narrow exception to fixed policies: only while no physical request exists and the stored deadline is null may reserve set a non-null deadline, with every other policy field unchanged. Player configuration before the first request therefore does not break the first host reservation. A consumed null policy remains null after restart; the host never starts a fresh clock for it. Lost-reply retries reuse their original chosen deadline.
